履修条件
授業概要
都市・建物・人体に関わる熱環境を対象として、物理現象をどのようにモデル化・観測・評価し、現代の環境問題や社会的課題の理解と解決に活用するかを学ぶ。都市微気候については、CFD、都市キャノピーモデル、メソスケール気象モデルなど、異なる空間スケールのモデルがどのような物理現象を表現し、何をパラメータ化しているかを学ぶ。建物については、EnergyPlusやTRNSYSに代表される物理モデルに加え、grey-box model、data-driven model、surrogate modelなどを取り上げ、物理的解釈性、計算負荷、予測精度、外挿性などの観点から各アプローチの特徴を比較する。また、衛星リモートセンシング、GIS、3次元都市データ、各種観測データを用いた都市熱環境の評価手法について学ぶ。
後半では、都市冷却技術、極端高温への適応と熱的レジリエンス、低所得・アフォーダブル住宅の温熱環境と省エネルギー、脱炭素と炭素収支など、近年重要性が高まっている研究課題を取り上げる。最新の研究論文を適宜紹介し、物理メカニズム、モデルの仮定、空間・時間スケール、評価指標の違いが研究結果やその解釈にどのような影響を与えるかを考察する。
This course examines how thermal processes in cities and buildings are modeled, observed, and evaluated, and how these methods can be applied to contemporary environmental and societal challenges. Urban microclimate modeling is introduced through computational fluid dynamics, urban canopy models, and mesoscale atmospheric models, with emphasis on the physical processes represented at different spatial scales and on the processes that must be parameterized. Building energy modeling is discussed from physics-based approaches such as EnergyPlus and TRNSYS to grey-box, data-driven, and surrogate models, highlighting differences in physical interpretability, computational cost, predictive performance, and extrapolation capability. The course also introduces methods for observing and mapping urban thermal environments using satellite remote sensing, GIS, three-dimensional urban data, and field measurements.
The latter part of the course focuses on current research topics including urban cooling technologies, adaptation and resilience to extreme heat, thermal and energy performance of affordable housing, and decarbonization and carbon balance. Recent research papers will be introduced throughout the course to examine how scientific conclusions are influenced by physical mechanisms, model assumptions, spatial and temporal scales, and the choice of evaluation metrics.

全体の教育目標
Upon successful completion of the course, students will be able to distinguish major modeling and observational approaches used for urban and building thermal environments and explain the physical processes that are explicitly represented or parameterized in different models.
個別の教育目標
授業計画
1. Modeling Urban Microclimate across Scales
2. Building Energy Modeling: Physics, Data, and Surrogate Models
3. Observing and Mapping Urban Thermal Environments
4. Urban Cooling Technologies and Their Physical Mechanisms
5. Extreme Heat Adaptation and Thermal Resilience
6. Thermal Environment, Energy, and Resilience in Affordable Housing
7. Decarbonization, Carbon Balance, and Environmental Trade-offs
